STEP 1 - Scene: This is a small snack of raw almonds on a white square plate, photographed from above (near top-down view). Not a full meal, just a handful of nuts.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square/rounded-square side plate, roughly 20 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 x (10)^2 ≈ 314 cm^2 (treating it as a circle-equivalent).

STEP 3 - Items: Raw almonds (about 25-28 whole nuts, some slightly split), plus one loose almond at the upper right.

STEP 4 - Area: The almond pile covers roughly 12-15% of the plate's area. Almonds are about 2.5 cm long and 1.5 cm wide, each lying flat, so individual almonds are about 3 cm^2 each. Twenty-seven almonds cover about 80-90 cm^2 when spread out, but the pile overlaps, so the visible footprint is about 40-45 cm^2 (roughly 13% of 314 cm^2).

STEP 5 - Volume: Pile height is about 1.2 cm (almonds are about 1 cm thick, with some stacking). Volume ≈ 42 cm^2 x 1.2 cm ≈ 50 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Almonds are dense, but whole nuts have large air gaps. Bulk density for whole nuts is about 0.5-0.6 g/ml. 50 ml x 0.55 ≈ 28 g. Counting pieces: 27 almonds x ~1.2 g each ≈ 32 g, which agrees. Use about 30 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw almonds are about 580 kcal per 100 g. 30 g x 5.8 ≈ 174 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 30 g (roughly a small handful, about one ounce) of almonds is typically around 170 kcal, which is plausible for this visible amount.
